outcome: Give eCommerce teams a working Demand Forecasting & Dynamic Pricing capability on their own data — it reduces capital in slow inventory and eliminates out-of-stocks.
overview: Online retailers pay for demand uncertainty at both ends: working capital sits in slow-moving inventory while high-demand lines sell out and lose the order permanently, and static prices leave margin uncollected in between. Demand Forecasting & Dynamic Pricing produces SKU-level forecasts from order, inventory, competitor-price and promotion data, then applies elasticity rules to recommend daily price points and replenishment plans. Recommendations reach the storefront through a control tower a merchandiser reviews, and the pricing guardrails stay the customer’s. Redington baselines forecast error and stockout rate on real trading history, then builds and instruments the pipeline over five to six weeks before production rollout is scoped separately.
